summary: This diff consolidates the previously-scattered Owner<->AI protocol/memory directive files into two canonical YAML files (PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml, MEMORY_OWNER_AI.yaml) and adds a real enforcement script (check_single_protocol_file.py) wired into preflight-guard.py to keep it that way; it is purely additive (no deletions in the diff, no .github/workflows/** changes, no migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security/.env paths touched), matching the tier1 classification. I independently verified rather than trusting the self-report: confirmed via git log that the three files claimed 'folded_and_deleted' (STANDING_OPERATING_PROTOCOL_2026-07-26.yaml, OWNER_ASSISTANT_RUNBOOK_2026-07-26.yaml, TASK_LIFECYCLE_STATE_MACHINE_2026-07-26.yaml) were never git-tracked in this repo to begin with (so their absence from the diff as deletions is expected, not a dropped edit) and directly listed /opt/veridian/ai-os/OWNER_DIRECTIVES/ on disk to confirm it now holds exactly the 2 new canonical YAML files plus the 4 retained .txt files, matching the PR's own source_inventory claims. I also executed check_single_protocol_file.py and the new preflight-guard.py hook directly against the live directory and confirmed both pass cleanly (exit 0, exactly 1 protocol + 1 memory file found), and confirmed the sys.path-based import between the two scripts resolves correctly. Code quality is good: safe YAML loading only, no shell/command injection, no eval, sensible fail-open-on-infra-error / fail-closed-on-real-drift semantics consistent with the existing crontab-drift check in the same file.
issues: Architecture/reliability risk (not a correctness bug): check_single_protocol_file() is unconditionally called for every single task dispatch server-wide (added to the unparameterized checks in preflight-guard.py's __main__), regardless of whether the dispatched task touches ai-os/OWNER_DIRECTIVES/ at all. Its classifier heuristic is loose (any top-level 'articles', 'incidents', or 'lessons' key, or meta.status == 'NON_NEGOTIABLE', on any .yaml/.yml file dropped into that one directory for an unrelated reason) triggers a hard fail-closed that would block ALL task dispatch on the server, not just work touching that directory, until manually diagnosed. This mirrors the existing crontab-drift check's fail-closed philosophy but has a wider and looser trigger surface -- worth tightening the signature or scoping the check only to tasks that touch that path in a future iteration.

Minor: _classify() fails open (returns None, i.e. 'not a candidate') on any YAML parse error, so a duplicate protocol/memory file with a syntax error would silently evade the drift check rather than being flagged as a problem needing attention -- low severity given the internal/non-adversarial threat model here.
No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff, so the hard rule against workflow-file changes in worker tasks does not apply here.
